report:
## Research Findings

The evidence base does **not** support "no" — the scientific consensus is that EMDR **does** alleviate PTSD symptoms.

**Efficacy evidence:** Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials show EMDR reduces PTSD diagnoses and symptom severity, with effects comparable to trauma-focused cognitive-behavioral therapy (TF-CBT) and superior to inactive controls like waitlist or usual care (https://www.psicothema.com/pdf/4820.pdf; https://www.emdria.org/resource/is-emdr-effective-for-improving-post-traumatic-stress-symptoms-in-people-with-post-traumatic-stress-disorders-an-overview-of-systematic-reviews-with-meta-analysis-european-journal-of-trauma-dissoc/). A Cochrane-linked network meta-analysis of psychological treatments for adult PTSD also places EMDR among the effective first-line options (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32284821/).

**Guideline endorsement:** EMDR is recommended as a first-line PTSD treatment by major bodies including the World Health Organization (2013), the UK's NICE, and the US VA/DoD, based on this accumulated trial evidence (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_movement_desensitization_and_reprocessing).

**Where the "no" intuition comes from:** The controversy isn't over whether EMDR helps, but over *why*. Critics (e.g., Lilienfeld, Lohr, McNally) argue the eye-movement/bilateral-stimulation component itself may not add unique therapeutic value beyond standard exposure therapy — the "active ingredient" is disputed even though overall symptom improvement is not (https://www.mrscsolutions.com/blog/why-is-emdr-so-controversial/). So skepticism concerns the *mechanism*, not the outcome.

## Conclusion
The evidence indicates EMDR **does** alleviate PTSD symptoms — this is well-supported by RCTs, meta-analyses, and endorsement from WHO/NICE/VA guidelines. If your source claimed otherwise, it likely conflated legitimate debate about EMDR's mechanism (whether eye movements are necessary) with its overall clinical effectiveness, which is not seriously disputed.
